title: Identification of Common Dysregulated Genes in COVID-19 and Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis: A Systems Biology and Machine Learning Approach.
authors: Dasgupta, Sanjukta; Das, Sankha Subhra; Patidar, Sankalp; Kajaria, Vaibhav; Chowdhury, Sushmita Roy; Chaudhury, Koel
journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过系统生物学和机器学习识别COVID-19与过敏性肺炎的共失调基因及转录因子，但核心是疾病诊断标志物，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制，仅边缘相关。
abstract: A comprehensive knowledge on systems biology of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 is crucial for differential diagnosis of COVID-19. Interestingly, the radiological and pathological features of COVID-19 mimic that of hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP), another pulmonary fibrotic phenotype. This motivated us to explore the overlapping pathophysiology of COVID-19 and HP, if any, and using a systems biology approach. Two datasets were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database (GSE147507 and GSE150910) and common differentially expressed genes (DEGs) for both diseases identified. Fourteen common DEGs, significantly altered in both diseases, were found to be implicated in complement activation and growth factor activity. A total of five microRNAs (hsa-miR-1-3p, hsa-miR-20a-5p, hsa-miR-107, hsa-miR-16-5p, and hsa-miR-34b-5p) and five transcription factors (KLF6, ZBTB7A, ELF1, NFIL3, and ZBT33) exhibited highest interaction with these common genes. Next, C3, CFB, MMP-9, and IL1A were identified as common hub genes for both COVID-19 and HP. Finally, these top-ranked genes (hub genes) were evaluated using random forest classifier to discriminate between the disease and control group (coronavirus disease 2019 [COVID-19] vs. controls, and HP vs. controls). This supervised machine learning approach demonstrated 100% and 87.6% accuracy in differentiating COVID-19 from controls, and HP from controls, respectively. These findings provide new molecular leads that inform COVID-19 and HP diagnostics and therapeutics research and innovation.
abstract_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的系统生物学全面知识对于COVID-19的鉴别诊断至关重要。有趣的是，COVID-19的放射学和病理学特征与过敏性肺炎（HP）相似，后者是另一种肺纤维化表型。这促使我们探索COVID-19与HP之间可能存在的重叠病理生理学，并采用系统生物学方法进行研究。从基因表达综合数据库（GSE147507和GSE150910）获取了两个数据集，并鉴定了两种疾病共有的差异表达基因（DEGs）。发现14个在两种疾病中均显著改变的共有DEGs涉及补体激活和生长因子活性。共有五个microRNAs（hsa-miR-1-3p、hsa-miR-20a-5p、hsa-miR-107、hsa-miR-16-5p和hsa-miR-34b-5p）和五个转录因子（KLF6、ZBTB7A、ELF1、NFIL3和ZBT33）与这些共有基因表现出最高的相互作用。接下来，C3、CFB、MMP-9和IL1A被鉴定为COVID-19和HP的共有枢纽基因。最后，使用随机森林分类器评估这些排名靠前的基因（枢纽基因），以区分疾病组和对照组（2019冠状病毒病[COVID-19]与对照组，以及HP与对照组）。这种监督机器学习方法在区分COVID-19与对照组以及HP与对照组方面分别展示了100%和87.6%的准确率。这些发现提供了新的分子线索，为COVID-19和HP的诊断与治疗研究及创新提供信息。
